subject: Request: hotpatch telemetry & CVE remediation evidence for SOC 2 review
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmebank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeBank Security <security@acmebank.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence request: hotpatch telemetry and CVE remediation (SOC 2)

Hi Sean —

We're preparing for an upcoming SOC 2 evidence collection and need to capture your vulnerability management posture for scoped systems. Specifically, can you provide the following items for the last three months: 

- Raw patch/hotpatch telemetry for any CVE remediations (CSV or similar) covering timestamps and host identifiers;
- A short attestation describing your SLA for critical CVEs (time-to-remediation), and any recent exceptions;
- Proof of remediation for CVE-2026-0456 (logs or signed manifest);
- Details on canary/staged rollouts (percentage, rollback criteria) and any observed rollbacks in the period.

We'd like the artifacts by EOD next Wednesday (26 Feb) to include them in the auditor bundle. If you need an extension or have questions about scope, let me know.

Thanks —
Laura Chen
Senior Information Security Manager
AcmeBank

P.S. If there's a single packaged file or a short narrative we can put in the SOC binder, that would be ideal.
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: hotpatch telemetry and CVE remediation (SOC 2)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide the telemetry and a signed attestation. I've looped in Kim (security engineering) for the technical proof and Monica (CS) to coordinate delivery to your secure drive.

High-level plan:
1) Kim will produce a short attestation and the CVE-2026-0456 remediation log (pdf).
2) We'll export the patch telemetry as CSV (redwood_patch_manifest_v1.csv) and a separate canary summary (canary-rollout-summary.txt).
3) Monica will upload to the HubSpot/Drive link you provided and share the download links and a signed cover letter.

Target delivery: Tue 24 Feb (initial bundle), final notarized attestation by Wed 26 Feb unless you need it sooner. Please confirm if Tue 24 is acceptable for a first pass.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
m: 415-555-0186
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmebank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: hotpatch telemetry and CVE remediation (SOC 2)

Laura / Sean —

Attaching the technical artifacts for the requested period. Summary below; full logs are in the attached files.

Summary of VM posture and evidence (concise):
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated vulnerability scans across host fleet + daily container image scans. High-severity findings triaged to owners within 24 hours of discovery; Critical CVEs are placed into the hotpatch playbook.
- SLA for Critical CVEs (AcmeBank Dedicated profile): 48-hour remediation window measured from creation of a verified exploitability ticket. For hosted customers our standard commitment is 72 hours; AcmeBank's environment is on Dedicated and is on the 48-hour track per contract.
- CVE-2026-0456: vulnerability discovered 2026-01-27 (internal scan). Hotpatch staged 2026-02-02; Canary rollout at 10% for 3 hours, expanded to 50% for 6 hours, then full rollout. No rollbacks were triggered. Evidence: cve-2026-0456-hotpatch-log.pdf (signed at bottom by Security), redwood_patch_manifest_v1.csv (per-host timestamps and patch IDs), canary-rollout-summary.txt (percentages and rollback-triggers).
- Exceptions: We observed a single customer-specific exception for a low-availability subsystem in Jan; that exception was logged and approved by our security review board (SRB). No SLA breaches for critical CVEs in the last 90 days.

Notes on telemetry: the CSV contains host_id, patch_id, applied_at (UTC), operator, and verification_hash. We've redacted internal-only hostnames and included mapping keys for auditor consumption. If you need a signed letter on company letterhead, we can produce one; Monica can coordinate.

Attachments: cve-2026-0456-hotpatch-log.pdf, redwood_patch_manifest_v1.csv, canary-rollout-summary.txt

Kimberly Park
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Internal note to Sean: I validated the hash values and attached the signed PDF; ready to ship once Monica confirms upload location.

Kim / Sean —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. I downloaded the CSV and the PDF and reviewed the canary summary. Two quick clarifying items before we put this in the binder: 

1) Canary details: can you confirm the exact traffic percentage used during the 50% stage (we see a range in the summary file, want to ensure we capture the point-in-time value)?
2) Attestation: our auditors request a signed attestation on company letterhead confirming the 48-hour critical CVE SLA for AcmeBank and that no critical SLA breaches occurred during the reporting window. Can you provide that by EOD Monday (1 Mar)?
